references.title: Clear instructions
references.text: Use explicit, internally consistent instructions relevant to the customer's request. A clear instruction states the information requested or the next step. Unclear context alone does not establish a communication fault.
interpretation_limits: Experimental, AI-assisted Memoria draft; not an ABCD guideline or authentic company policy.
Assess only documented wording patterns and tested equivalents; unfamiliar wording is not a fault.
Do not penalise dialect, informal wording or minor grammar by themselves.

references.title: Respectful wording
references.text: Do not direct an explicit personal insult at the customer. Distinguish an agent assertion from quoted or reported speech and negation. Informal wording is not a communication fault.
interpretation_limits: Experimental, AI-assisted Memoria draft; not an ABCD guideline or authentic company policy.
A recognised insult must be the agent's own direct assertion, not a quotation, report or negation.
Do not infer personality, intent, emotion or vocal tone. An apology does not erase an established insult.

references.title: Acknowledge the request
references.text: Acknowledge the customer's stated request with a relevant paraphrase or direct response. Do not infer the customer's feelings or satisfaction. An apology or a prescribed empathy phrase is not required.
interpretation_limits: Experimental, AI-assisted Memoria draft; not an ABCD guideline or authentic company policy.
A response can acknowledge a request without establishing transaction completion.
Missing or unfamiliar acknowledgement wording alone does not prove the request was ignored.
